mainTopic: זבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן: offerings slaughtered with the wrong intent, and why they stay holy
overview: The first משנה of מסכת זבחים deals with a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמה, meaning the person slaughtering had a different kind of קרבן in mind. The תנא קמא rules that most קרבנות stay כשר, but the owner has not fulfilled his obligation. The exceptions are the פסח and the חטאת, which become פסול. רבי אליעזר adds the אשם, since it also comes for a sin. יוסי בן חוני says any קרבן slaughtered in the name of a פסח or a חטאת is פסול. שמעון אחי עזריה says it depends on whether the intended קרבן is holier or less holy, and the משנה gives examples. The גמרא then asks why the משנה says 'אלא שלא עלו' and answers that the קרבן stays holy, so the rest of its עבודה may not be done for the wrong purpose, matching a ruling of רבא. The גמרא supports this first with a סברא and then begins a proof from a פסוק, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Offerings slaughtered for the wrong purpose are valid, except פסח and חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמה is כשר, but it does not count toward the owner's obligation. The פסח and the חטאת are exceptions and become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All offerings that were slaughtered not for their own sake are valid. However, they do not count for the owners as fulfilling their obligation. The exceptions are the פסח and the חטאת. The פסח is invalid when this happens at its proper time, and the חטאת is invalid at any time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the מסכת with a basic rule. If someone slaughters a קרבן while intending it as a different קרבן, it is still כשר, but the owner must bring another one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate results here. The קרבן itself is still valid and its עבודה continues, but the owner's חובה is not fulfilled. For the פסח and the חטאת, wrong intent makes the קרבן itself פסול. The פסח is only affected during its set time, while the חטאת is affected all year.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Not for their own sake: slaughtered with intent for a different קרבן
Valid: the קרבן may be offered
Did not count for the owners as their obligation
The Paschal offering
Sin offering

steps.confusionAlert: "כשרים" does not mean everything is fine. The קרבן is valid, but the owner still has to bring a new one to fulfill his obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the base for the whole first פרק of זבחים. It separates two questions: whether the קרבן is valid, and whether the owner has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
All offerings that were slaughtered not for their own sake
are valid,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה;
phrases.english: but they did not count for the owners as their obligation;
except for the Pesach and the Chatas:
the Pesach at its time,
and the Chatas at any time.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמה is כשר but does not fulfill the owner's obligation. A פסח in its time and a חטאת at any time become פסול.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר adds the אשם to the exceptions
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו is also פסול, just like a חטאת, at any time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: The אשם too. The פסח is invalid at its time, and the חטאת and the אשם are invalid at any time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the תנא קמא and adds a third exception: the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, an אשם slaughtered with the wrong intent stays כשר. רבי אליעזר puts the אשם together with the חטאת: both are פסול all year, while the פסח is only affected in its time.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering
Also, too
At any time of the year

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: The Asham too;
the Pesach at its time,
and the Chatas and the Asham at any time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא by adding the אשם to the list of exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו is פסול at any time.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's reason: חטאת and אשם both come for a sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר compares the אשם to the חטאת, since both are brought because of a sin. If a חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה, so is an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: The חטאת comes for a sin, and the אשם comes for a sin. Just as a חטאת is invalid when slaughtered not for its sake, so too the אשם is invalid when slaughtered not for its sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר explains why the אשם belongs on the list. He compares it to the חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared feature is that both קרבנות come to atone for a sin. Everyone agrees a חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה, so רבי אליעזר applies the same rule to the אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes because of a sin
Just as ... so too: a comparison that carries a rule from one case to another
Invalid

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
The Chatas comes for a sin,
and the Asham comes for a sin;
just as a Chatas is invalid not for its sake,
so too the Asham is invalid not for its sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: הַחַטָּאת בָּאָה עַל חֵטְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו is פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to the חטאת, since both come because of a sin, and a חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה.

steps.title: יוסי בן חוני: offerings slaughtered as a פסח or חטאת are invalid
steps.stepSummary: יוסי בן חוני adds that other קרבנות slaughtered in the name of a פסח or a חטאת are also פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: יוסי בן חוני says: Offerings slaughtered for the sake of a פסח or for the sake of a חטאת are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: יוסי בן חוני adds another case. This time the problem is not the קרבן being slaughtered but the name it was slaughtered in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא only discussed a פסח or a חטאת that was slaughtered for another purpose. יוסי בן חוני also covers the reverse: a regular קרבן slaughtered with the intent that it be a פסח or a חטאת is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Those that are slaughtered
For the sake of, in the name of
Invalid (plural)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the פסח and חטאת are the intended name, not the animal actually being slaughtered. He is talking about other קרבנות.

phrases.english: Yosei ben Choni says:

phrases.aramaic: הַנִּשְׁחָטִין לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח וּלְשֵׁם חַטָּאת – פְּסוּלִין.
phrases.english: Those slaughtered for the sake of a Pesach or for the sake of a Chatas are invalid.
phrases.notes: He means other offerings that someone slaughtered while thinking of them as a פסח or a חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case: the wrong intent is the name of a פסח or a חטאת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any קרבן slaughtered לשם פסח or לשם חטאת is פסול.

steps.title: שמעון אחי עזריה: higher holiness is valid, lower is invalid
steps.stepSummary: שמעון אחי עזריה says the result depends on the level of holiness of the intended קרבן. If it is higher, the קרבן is כשר. If it is lower, the קרבן is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון אחי עזריה says: If he slaughtered them for the sake of an offering higher than them, they are valid. If for the sake of one lower than them, they are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: שמעון אחי עזריה offers a different way to decide when wrong intent makes a קרבן פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, the question is not which specific קרבן was involved but the direction of the mistake. Intending a holier קרבן keeps it כשר. Intending a less holy קרבן makes it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Higher than them: a קרבן with greater holiness
Lower than them: a קרבן with lesser holiness
He slaughtered them

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives four views on a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמה. The תנא קמא: valid, except the פסח and the חטאת. רבי אליעזר: the אשם too. יוסי בן חוני: any קרבן slaughtered in the name of a פסח or a חטאת is פסול. שמעון אחי עזריה: higher holiness is כשר, lower holiness is פסול.

phrases.english: Shimon, brother of Azarya, says:
If he slaughtered them for the sake of one higher than them, they are valid;
phrases.notes: Higher here means a קרבן with a greater level of holiness.

phrases.english: for the sake of one lower than them, they are invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another rule that decides by the holiness level of the intended קרבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent for a holier קרבן leaves it כשר. Intent for a less holy קרבן makes it פסול.

steps.title: Examples of the holier-versus-less-holy rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives examples of שמעון אחי עזריה's rule. קדשי קדשים slaughtered for קדשים קלים are פסול, and the reverse is כשר. Likewise, a בכור or מעשר slaughtered for שלמים is כשר, while שלמים slaughtered for a בכור or מעשר are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Offerings of the highest holiness that one slaughtered for the sake of offerings of lesser holiness are unfit. Offerings of lesser holiness that one slaughtered for the sake of offerings of the highest holiness are fit. The firstborn and the tithe that one slaughtered for the sake of a peace offering are fit. Peace offerings that one slaughtered for the sake of a firstborn or a tithe are unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is explaining שמעון אחי עזריה's rule from Step 5 by giving concrete cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Aiming 'up' to a holier קרבן is fine, but aiming 'down' to a less holy one makes the קרבן פסול. This works at two levels. Between קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים, the higher group wins. Inside קדשים קלים itself, שלמים rank higher than בכור and מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the highest holiness (like חטאת and עולה)
Offerings of lesser holiness (like שלמים)
A firstborn animal brought as a קרבן
The animal tithe, every tenth animal, brought as a קרבן
Peace offerings

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמעון אחי עזריה, slaughtering for a holier קרבן is כשר, and slaughtering for a less holy קרבן is פסול. Even within קדשים קלים, שלמים rank above בכור and מעשר.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't flip it! Aiming at a HIGHER קרבן keeps it כשר. Aiming at a LOWER קרבן makes it פסול.

phrases.english: How so?
Offerings of the highest holiness that one slaughtered
for the sake of offerings of lesser holiness are unfit;
offerings of lesser holiness that one slaughtered
for the sake of offerings of the highest holiness are fit.
The firstborn and the tithe that one slaughtered
for the sake of a peace offering are fit;
peace offerings that one slaughtered
for the sake of a firstborn or for the sake of a tithe are unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives concrete examples of the general rule stated in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering for a holier קרבן keeps it כשר. Slaughtering for a less holy קרבן makes it פסול. This applies both between holiness groups and within קדשים קלים.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'but' instead of 'and'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by questioning the wording of the משנה. Why did it say 'אלא שלא עלו' ('but they did not count') instead of the simpler 'ולא עלו' ('and they did not count')?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why do I need the משנה to teach 'but they did not count'? Let it simply teach 'and they did not count for the owner's obligation'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and challenges the wording of the משנה's first line. It asks what the extra word אלא ('but') is adding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every word in the משנה has a purpose. 'ולא עלו' would have said the same basic thing, so the word אלא must be teaching something extra. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need (this wording)?
Let it teach (simpler wording)
For the owners
Toward the owner's obligation

phrases.english: Gemara:
Why do I need it to teach
"but they did not count"?
phrases.notes: He is quoting the משנה's opening line from Step 1: the קרבן is כשר, 'but' it doesn't count for the owner.

phrases.english: Let it teach "and they did not count
for the owner's obligation"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the end of the משנה and goes back to examine the wording of its first line.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word אלא in the משנה's first ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler phrase, ולא עלו, would have taught the basic law, so the extra word seems unnecessary.

steps.title: It only fails for the owner but stays holy
steps.stepSummary: The word אלא teaches that the only problem is that the קרבן does not count for the owner. It keeps its holiness, so it is forbidden to change its purpose during the rest of the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that it is only for the owner that they did not count toward the obligation. But they remain in their holiness, and it is forbidden to change their purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The word 'but' limits the problem: the קרבן loses only its credit for the owner, and nothing else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלא means 'the only thing missing is...' So the קרבן is still fully holy as its original type. That is why the remaining steps, like the זריקה, must still be done for the correct purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
They remain in their holiness
To change (the purpose of the קרבן)

steps.whyThisMatters: The קרבן stays holy even after one wrong intention. So the כהן must keep doing the rest of the עבודה for its proper purpose.

phrases.english: This teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: לַבְּעָלִים הוּא דְּלָא עָלוּ לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה –
phrases.english: it is only for the owner that they did not count toward the obligation,
but they remain in their holiness,
and it is forbidden to change their purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that the extra word carries a legal lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without אלא, one might think a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמה loses its special status, so its purpose could freely be changed afterward.
steps.terutzMaskana: אלא limits the loss to the owner's credit only. The קרבן stays holy, and changing its purpose is forbidden.

steps.title: This matches רבא's ruling about an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this lesson fits רבא's ruling. Even after an עולה was slaughtered שלא לשמה, it is forbidden to do the זריקה of its blood שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is like רבא, as רבא said: A burnt offering that one slaughtered not for its sake, it is forbidden to sprinkle its blood not for its sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the lesson from the word אלא to a known ruling of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that once the שחיטה was done שלא לשמה, nothing more can go wrong. רבא says otherwise. The עולה is still holy, so the זריקה must still be done for its proper name, just as the word אלא teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: And this matches the view of רבא
Burnt offering
To sprinkle its blood on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: A קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמה is still holy. Only the owner's credit is lost. The remaining עבודה, like the זריקה, must still be done לשמה, as רבא rules.

phrases.english: And this is like רבא,
as רבא said:
a burnt offering that one slaughtered not for its sake,
it is forbidden to sprinkle its blood not for its sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 8 with a matching ruling from רבא.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמה stays holy and its purpose may not be changed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling that the blood of an עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה may not be sprinkled שלא לשמה.

steps.title: Two supports offered, starting with common sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the rule can be supported by a סברא or by a קרא. The סברא: if the כהן already changed the purpose once, should he keep changing it in all the other steps too?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, use logic, and if you want, use a פסוק. The logic: just because he changed the purpose once, should he go on and change it in all the rest of the steps?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that it has two ways to support the rule that the rest of the עבודה must still be done לשמה, and then gives the first one: plain logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from the word אלא, and רבא's ruling, say the קרבן keeps its holiness after a שלא לשמה slaughter. The סברא explains why: one wrong change in the שחיטה does not free the rest of the עבודה to be done for the wrong purpose. Making one wrong change is no excuse to make more.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces one of two possible answers or supports
A logical argument, common sense
A פסוק, a verse from the תורה
He changed, he went against the proper way

phrases.english: If you want, say a logical argument,
if you want, say a verse.
If you want, say a logical argument:
because he changed it once,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן who slaughtered the קרבן for the wrong purpose.

phrases.english: should he go on and change it in all these other steps too?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא, אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a logical reason for the rule from Step 8, which רבא's ruling in Step 9 matches.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that after a שלא לשמה slaughter, the rest of the עבודה may not be done שלא לשמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A סברא: one change does not permit further changes.

steps.title: The second support: a פסוק about keeping promises
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק 'מוצא שפתיך תשמר ועשית' and starts to read it closely, asking how the פסוק can call a vow (נדרת) a נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, use a פסוק: 'That which goes out of your lips you shall keep and do, according to what you vowed to ה׳ your God as a gift offering, etc.' Is this really a נדבה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its second support, a פסוק, and opens with a question about the wording. It is setting up a derivation that will be finished in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'נדרת', you vowed, but then calls it a 'נדבה', a gift offering. A נדר and a נדבה are two different kinds of pledge, so the mix seems strange. The גמרא's question 'האי נדבה?!' points at this oddness, which it will use to learn the lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: What comes out of your lips: what you promised
You vowed: from the word נֶדֶר
A voluntary gift offering

phrases.english: If you want, say a verse:
"That which goes out of your lips you shall keep and do,
according to what you vowed to ה׳ your God
as a gift offering, etc."
Is this a gift offering?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא: מוֹצָא שְׂפָתֶיךָ תִּשְׁמֹר וְעָשִׂיתָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the two promised supports, after the סברא in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמה keeps its holiness and must still be offered properly.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in דברים 23:24, read closely starting with its odd wording 'נדרת... נדבה'.
